Google OKF in Practice: Persistent Memory and Knowledge Patterns for AI Agents

The video features the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) 0.2, a plain text format to store knowledge, and the OKF Agent Memory project, which uses the format as a persistent memory for AI agents. Explains the five-layer architecture, agent rules and commands to use on a daily basis.

Amnesia of AI agents

The video deals with a common problem: the AI agent forgets the context of architecture in the middle of a code session 00:00. The proposal is a simple text pattern, supported by Google, to give the agent a long-term memory 00:20.

During a session, the agent receives instructions, makes architectural decisions and discovers the context of the domain. When the context window closes, everything disappears 01:02. A persistent memory layer that does not depend on a specific company is missing 01:23.

Today, the options are bad 01:43:

  • Improvised, structureless Markdown files that swell the context window and spend tokens 01:43.
  • Vector, expensive, opaque databases that create supplier dependency 01:43.

What is OKF

Open Knowledge Format, version 0.2, was announced by Google Cloud in June 2026. 02:25. It is not a software nor a database: it is an open and neutral specification 02:25. Knowledge is in a Markdown file directory with YAML header 02:25. The only mandatory field is the type 02:47.

Video compares OKF to a knowledge USB-C cable: a common format that any AI can read, write and exchange without a different SDK for each project 03:07.

The design follows three principles 03:29:

  • be minimally opinative, without imposing rigid structures 03:29;
  • separate who produces from who consumes: a decision written by an AI can be read months later in a common text editor 03:29;
  • focus on format, not the platform 03:49.

The architecture

Everything stays in a knowledge bundle, which is a common directory tree 04:10. Each concept has a Markdown file with a unique ID, metadata at the top, text body and links to other concepts 04:10. With simple Markdown links, agents follow the knowledge network as a graph, no database 04:31.

The system has five layers 04:52:

1. the OKF specification 04:52; 2. the conventions of memory 04:52; 3. Agent skills and prompts 04:52; 4. tools, which validate the files 04:52; 5. knowledge of the project 05:12.

Separate the layers strip from the model work with formatting: the tool ensures the structure 05:12.

The OKF agent

OKF Agent Memory takes the format to Git as an agent memory 05:12. According to the video, the search takes less than 300 microseconds, with BM25 indexes, in a Go binary without external dependencies 05:33. Project says it reduces token waste by 80% 05:54. This comes from the progressive disclosure: the AI consults the indexes and carries only the concepts it needs 06:16.

The officer follows strict rules 06:16:

  • search before writing 06:16;
  • prefer updating a file to creating a duplicate 06:16;
  • mark the source of the data 06:37;
  • explicitly say when you're not sure about something 06:37.

In practice

The main commands are 06:58:

  • okf bootstrap, which configures the memory base of the project 06:58;
  • okf validate, which checks whether the files follow the specification 06:58;
  • okf search, to seek 07:19;
  • okf createTo create a concept 07:19.

Every memory change goes through Git and goes into normal code review 07:19. Command okf mcp climbs an MCP server by default input and output without opening network port 07:39. The context gets private on the local machine and connects to editors like Cursor, Codex and Claude, without network API cost 07:39.

The Future of Knowledge

The video contrasts proprietary, fragile and opaque vector stores with simple text knowledge packages, Git natives and auditable by anyone 08:20. The final question is whether the organization's knowledge will be readable by the agents of the future or will be stuck in a black box 08:40.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is OKF a database?

Nope. It is an open specification: a Markdown file directory with YAML header 02:25.

Which field is required in an OKF concept?

Only the field type 02:47.

Do I need a cloud server to use OKF memory?

Nope. According to the video, the MCP server runs on the local machine, by input and default output 07:39.

Reviewed by Maurício Yokoyama Issei in 19 November 2026.

About the video

In this explanatory video, we explore the **Google Open Knowledge Format (OKF)** and demonstrate how to use the ecosystem **okf-agent-memory** in practice!

**OKF** is an open and seller-neutral specification that formalizes organizational knowledge in a Markdown file structure enriched with YAML (frontmatter) metadata. It solves the fragmented context problem in AI systems, creating a navigable knowledge graph, versioned in Git and directly readable by humans and AI agents, without the need for complex vector databases.

We deepen the updates of the version **OKF v0.2**, which introduces signs of trust, traceability of provenance (`generated`, `verified`, `sources`), life cycle management (`status`, `stale after`) and certified computing.

In addition, we present the ecosystem **okf-agent-memory**, developed in Go with search BM25 in high speed memory (less than 300μs) and embedded MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for direct integration with tools such as Claude Code and Cursor.
